Points are J1-judged refusal rates from the Experiment~9 RefusEU-TRAIN probe, with the Hautus correction $(k+0.5)/(n+1)$ used in the Experiment~9 analysis. Shaded bands are Wilson 95\\% intervals on the raw proportion. $n=300$ harmful items at $\\lambda=0$ and the 100-item core block at every $\\lambda>0$. Gemma's Slovene curve lies to the right of its English curve throughout the transition (0.64 vs.\\ 0.32 at $\\lambda=1$): at each dose, more Slovene refusal remains. GaMS3's Slovene curve lies only slightly above its English curve (largest gap 0.14, at $\\lambda=0.5$), and the two meet near the floor from $\\lambda=1$ onward. These per-dose gaps are descriptive. The pre-registered cross-model comparison is made at matched English refusal, not at matched dose.}\n\\label{fig:dose}\n\\end{figure}\n\nFigure~\\ref{fig:dose} plots refusal rate against abliteration dose for both models.\nExperiment~9 measures refusal rates across nine $\\lambda$ values for both models in English and Slovene (300 items per condition).\nGemma's dose-response curve in Slovene is right-shifted relative to its English curve: at matched doses, more Slovene refusal remains.\nGaMS3 shows a smaller shift.\nThe fine-grained 13-step dose ladder (Experiment~15) gives the most powerful estimate: $\\mathrm{G3} = -0.70$ $[-1.01, -0.42]$ with a minimum detectable effect of 0.42.\nThe edit-induced component is $+0.47$ $[-0.96, 2.14]$, consistent with zero: the cross-model gap is baseline, not edit-induced.\n\n\\subsection{Inconclusive and Null Results}\n\n\\paragraph{Unedited cross-model gap at Slovene-to-Slovene prompts.}\nExperiment~15 gives $\\mathrm{G3}_{\\text{orig}} = -1.17$ $[-2.83, 0.22]$.\nThis is a ceiling artefact: its fragility index, the number of item reclassifications needed to move the CI boundary past zero, is 1 (a single item reclassification in the Gemma $\\lambda\\text{-}0$ Slovene cell, where 299 of 300 items are refused, moves it inside the margin).\nOnly the Experiment~9 body has a robust offset (fragility index 9).\n\n\\paragraph{Hungarian.}\nAll Hungarian contrasts are uninformative.\nThe minimum detectable effect is approximately 3 log-odds units.\n\n\\paragraph{Experiment~16 zero-dose.}\nThe Experiment~16 zero-dose Gemma criterion DiD is $-0.65$ $[-0.90, -0.46]$, rated ESTIMATE.\nIt is not a confirmation of the Experiment~5 headline because it uses a different item body, a different judge, and a different design (suffix-based output-language manipulation vs paired translation).\n\n\\paragraph{RefusEU validation.}\nExperiment~17 tests attack success rate on 1,300 EN $+$ 1,300 SL RefusEU prompts.\nThe edit is effective in all four model $\\times$ language cells (ROBUST), with ASR deltas of 0.657--0.937.\nThe EN-vs-SL within-model difference is not interpretable as a language effect because the prompt sets are different natural prompts (LaBSE similarity 0.55).\n\n\\section{Discussion}\n\\label{sec:discussion}\n\n\\subsection{Interpretation}\n\nThe criterion-shift measurement has a concrete interpretation for multilingual evaluation: a model can appear ``safer'' in a non-English language because it refuses more benign requests, inflating the refusal rate without any improvement in harm detection.\nThe SDT framing separates these two components.\nThe near-zero DiD on $d'$ means that the language shift does not make either model better or worse at distinguishing harmful from benign items; the measured difference is in the threshold.\n\\citet{Aziz2026} described a similar calibration-not-representation pattern across 23 languages; the present sibling-pair design adds GaMS3-specific detail but does not change the interpretation.\n\nThe reply-language finding, if confirmed by future work with validated judge anchors, would suggest that Gemma's refusal mechanism interacts with output-language processing.\n\\citet{Upadhyaya2026} showed that safety features are geometrically entangled with language-identity features; the present study's $3{\\times}3$ design separates the input and output dimensions but cannot determine the mechanism.\n\n\\subsection{Limitations}\n\n\\paragraph{ESTIMATE rating on the primary finding.}\nThe criterion-shift DiD reverses sign ($-0.31$) when partial answers are coded as refusals.\nThe choice of coding rule therefore determines whether over-refusal is attributed to Gemma or is absent.\nThis fragility bounds how strongly the finding can be stated.\n\n\\paragraph{Judge quality.}\nThe Qwen3-14B judge for Experiment~5 was calibrated against gemini-2.5-flash on DEV ($\\kappa$ 0.68--0.86) but not against human labels.\nOn edited rows across the study, no judge exceeds $\\kappa = 0.51$ against blind adjudication.\nThe readout gate has never passed.\nAll adjudication in this study is author-model LLM, not human review.\n\n\\paragraph{Sample size.}\nThe adjudication sample is 30 items per cell for benign false-refusal rates, limiting precision.\nThe refusal-composition numbers (54\\% explicit, 26\\% deflection) come from $n = 50$ high-dose harmful items.\n\n\\paragraph{Language compliance.}\nFour GaMS3 cells fall below 90\\% compliance (SL$\\to$EN at 0.00, HU$\\to$EN at 0.14, SL$\\to$HU at 0.56, HU$\\to$SL at 0.86).\nGaMS3 did not follow the output-language instruction off the English-input row; its SL$\\to$EN responses were written in Slovene, not English.\nMechanism claims for GaMS3 are therefore restricted to the compliant EN-input row.\n\n\\paragraph{Quantization.}\nBoth models run in NF4 (4-bit) quantization, which may affect refusal behaviour relative to full-precision weights.\n\n\\paragraph{Novelty.}\nThe observation that over-refusal rates differ across languages is partially anticipated by \\citet{Addagada2026} and \\citet{Nguyen2026}.\nThe present work's contribution is the signal-detection decomposition and the controlled sibling-pair design.\n\n\\section{Conclusion}\n\nUnedited Gemma-3-12B-IT false-refuses benign Slovene items at 0.569 vs 0.364 in English.\nSignal-detection analysis attributes this to a criterion shift ($\\mathrm{DiD}_c = +0.52$ $[0.38, 0.68]$) with no sensitivity difference.\nThe finding is rated ESTIMATE because the sign reverses under an alternative coding rule.\nOn edited models, the criterion difference is inconclusive (0.14 $[-0.78, 1.12]$).\nA secondary analysis of reply-language refusal yields a PPI-corrected output-language effect of $+2.43$ $[+0.89, +5.38]$ for Gemma, but this is also rated ESTIMATE because the harmful-content adjudicator $\\kappa$ is 0.12.\nMultilingual safety evaluations that report only attack-success rates on harmful items will miss criterion shifts that inflate refusal rates on benign items.\n\n\\bibliographystyle{plainnat}\n\\bibliography{references}\n\n\\end{document}", """Read the run's output files and write the JSON blocks the interactive page embeds."""
import json, random, collections, math
from statistics import NormalDist
E = '/ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_FVi3e3O9CH5I/3_invention_loop'
X5 = E + '/iter_2/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_5'
X14 = E + '/iter_4/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_14'
X9 = E + '/iter_3/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_9'
EV5 = E + '/iter_5/gen_art/gen_art_evaluation_5'
out = {}
TRUNC = 400

# ---------- exp5: SDT settings ----------
a5 = json.load(open(X5 + '/results/analysis_final.json'))['C2_hard_sdt']
keep = ['primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT', 'SLMT_vs_ENorig', 'xstest_only', 'orbench_only', 'mt_fragile_dropped', 'primary_Rp']
settings = {}
for k in keep:
    v = a5[k]
    settings[k] = {
        'cells': v['cells'],  # order: gemma EN, gemma SL, gams EN, gams SL
        'DiD_c': {'est': v['DiD_c']['est'], 'ci95': v['DiD_c']['ci95']},
        'DiD_dprime': {'est': v['DiD_dprime']['est'], 'ci95': v['DiD_dprime']['ci95']},
        'n_safe': v.get('n_safe'), 'n_unsafe': v.get('n_unsafe'),
    }
p = a5['primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT']
settings['primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT']['own_delta'] = p['own_delta']
settings['primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT']['mcnemar'] = p['mcnemar_within_model_SL_vs_EN']
out['sdt'] = settings

# ---------- exp5: per-item HARD records ----------
rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open(X5 + '/results/items_final.jsonl')]
hard = [r for r in rows if r['set'] == 'hard' and r['arm'] in ('EN_BT', 'SL_MT', 'EN_orig')]
code = {'REFUSE': 'R', 'PARTIAL': 'P', 'COMPLY': 'C', None: '-'}
items = collections.OrderedDict()
for r in hard:
    it = items.setdefault(r['item_id'], {'id': r['item_id'], 'src': r['source'], 'type': r['xstest_type'],
                                         'harm': 1 if r['is_harmful'] else 0, 'frag': 1 if r['mt_fragile'] else 0,
                                         'cat': r['category'], 'lab': {}, 'txt': {}, 'chrf': None})
    assert it['harm'] == (1 if r['is_harmful'] else 0) and it['frag'] == (1 if r['mt_fragile'] else 0)
    m = 'g' if r['model'] == 'gemma_it' else 'm'
    arm = {'EN_BT': 'E', 'SL_MT': 'S', 'EN_orig': 'O'}[r['arm']]
    it['lab'][m + arm] = code[r['judge_primary']]
    it['txt']['p' + arm] = r['prompt_text']
    if arm in 'ES':
        it['txt'][m + arm] = r['response']
        it['txt'][m + arm + 'n'] = r['n_new_tokens']
    if r['bt_chrf'] is not None: it['chrf'] = r['bt_chrf']
items = list(items.values())
print('hard items', len(items), collections.Counter(i['harm'] for i in items))

def R(lab, partial_refuse=False):
    return 1 if lab == 'R' or (partial_refuse and lab == 'P') else 0

# subset rule for embedded text
rng = random.Random(20260925)
benign = [i for i in items if not i['harm']]
harm = [i for i in items if i['harm']]
disc = [i for i in benign if R(i['lab']['gS']) != R(i['lab']['gE']) or R(i['lab']['mS']) != R(i['lab']['mE'])]
rest = [i for i in benign if i not in disc]
pick = set(i['id'] for i in disc) | set(i['id'] for i in rng.sample(rest, 100)) | set(i['id'] for i in rng.sample(harm, 60))
compact = []
for i in items:
    lab = ''.join(i['lab'][k] for k in ['gE', 'gS', 'gO', 'mE', 'mS', 'mO'])
    rec = [i['id'], {'xstest': 'x', 'orbench_hard1k': 'h', 'orbench_toxic': 't'}[i['src']], i['type'] or '', i['harm'], i['frag'], lab]
    if i['id'] in pick:
        t = i['txt']
        def tr(s):
            return s if len(s) <= TRUNC else s[:TRUNC].rstrip() + '…'
        rec.append({'pO': t['pO'], 'pE': t['pE'], 'pS': t['pS'], 'chrf': i['chrf'],
                    'gE': tr(t['gE']), 'gS': tr(t['gS']), 'mE': tr(t['mE']), 'mS': tr(t['mS']),

table.num th:first-child,table.num td:first-child{text-align:left}
table.num thead th{font-weight:600;color:var(--ink);border-bottom:1.5px solid var(--rule)}
.tscroll{overflow-x:auto}
.note{font-size:15px;color:var(--muted)}
/* terms */
.term{font:inherit;color:inherit;background:none;border:0;padding:0 1px;border-bottom:1.5px dotted var(--accent);cursor:help;position:relative;min-height:0}
.termwrap{position:relative;display:inline}
.def{position:absolute;left:0;top:calc(100% + 6px);z-index:120;width:min(320px,80vw);background:#1b1b1f;color:#fff;font-size:14.5px;line-height:1.45;font-weight:400;padding:9px 12px;border-radius:8px;box-shadow:0 6px 18px rgba(0,0,0,.2);display:none;text-align:left;text-transform:none;letter-spacing:0}
.def.on{display:block}
/* stepper */
.stepper{outline:none}
ol.stagebtns{list-style:none;display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:6px;padding:0;margin:0 0 12px}
ol.stagebtns button{min-height:44px;min-width:44px;padding:4px 12px;border-radius:22px;border:1.5px solid #b9b6ad;background:#fff;font:inherit;font-size:15px;cursor:pointer;color:var(--ink2)}
ol.stagebtns button[aria-current="step"]{border-color:var(--accent);background:var(--accent);color:#fff;font-weight:600}
.stagebody{min-height:260px}
.stagegrid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr);gap:12px}
@media (min-width:760px){.stagegrid.cols2{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr))}}
.io{border:1px solid var(--rule);border-radius:10px;padding:10px 12px;background:#fdfdfb}
.io .h{font-size:13px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.05em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--muted);margin-bottom:4px}
.resp{font-size:15.5px;white-space:pre-wrap;word-break:break-word;max-height:220px;overflow:auto}
.stepnav{display:flex;gap:10px;align-items:center;margin-top:14px;flex-wrap:wrap}
.stepnav button{min-height:44px;padding:6px 18px;border-radius:8px;border:1.5px solid var(--accent);background:#fff;color:var(--accent);font:inherit;font-weight:600;cursor:pointer}
.stepnav button:disabled{border-color:#cfccc4;color:#a9a7a0;cursor:not-allowed}
.chip{display:inline-block;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:12px;letter-spacing:.03em}
.chip.R{background:#fde8dc;color:#8a2d05}
.chip.P{background:#fdf5d7;color:#6b4e00}
.chip.C{background:#e3f1e8;color:#1f5a33}
/* browser */
.browser{display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr);gap:16px}
@media (min-width:920px){.browser{grid-template-columns:minmax(0,340px) minmax(0,1fr)}}
ul.itemlist{list-style:none;margin:0;padding:0;max-height:560px;overflow:auto;border:1px solid var(--rule);border-radius:10px;background:#fff}
ul.itemlist li{border-bottom:1px solid var(--grid)}
ul.itemlist button{display:block;width:100%;text-align:left;min-height:48px;padding:8px 12px;border:0;background:none;font:inherit;font-size:15px;color:var(--ink);cursor:pointer}
ul.itemlist button[aria-pressed="true"]{background:var(--accent-soft);box-shadow:inset 4px 0 0 var(--accent)}
ul.itemlist .meta{display:block;font-size:13px;color:var(--muted);margin-top:2px}
.detail .prompts{display:grid;gap:8px;margin-bottom:12px}
.pl{font-size:13px;color:var(--muted);font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.04em;text-transform:uppercase}
.cellgrid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr);gap:10px}
@media (min-width:640px){.cellgrid{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr))}}
.cellbox{border:1px solid var(--rule);border-radius:10px;padding:10px 12px;background:#fff}
.cellbox.flag{border-color:var(--sl);box-shadow:0 0 0 1px var(--sl) inset}
.cellbox .top{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:center;gap:8px;margin-bottom:6px;font-weight:600;font-size:15px}
.more{margin-top:8px}
.more button{min-height:44px;padding:6px 14px;border-radius:8px;border:1.5px solid var(--accent);background:#fff;color:var(--accent);font:inherit;font-weight:600;cursor:pointer}
.panels{display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr);gap:18px}
@media (min-width:820px){.panels.two-up{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr))}}
.readout{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(150px,1fr));gap:10px;margin-top:10px}
.readout div{background:#f4f3ee;border-radius:8px;padding:8px 10px;font-size:15px}
.readout b{display:block;font-size:20px;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
ul.lims li{margin-bottom:8px}
footer{padding:36px 0 60px;background:var(--card)}
footer h2{font-size:24px}
dl.gloss dt{font-weight:700;margin-top:10px}
dl.gloss dd{margin:2px 0 0 0;color:var(--ink2)}
ul.prov li{margin-bottom:6px;font-size:16px}
code{font-family:var(--mono);font-size:.88em;background:#f0efe9;padding:1px 5px;border-radius:4px;word-break:break-all}
.sr{position:absolute;width:1px;height:1px;overflow:hidden;clip:rect(0 0 0 0);white-space:nowrap}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<a class="skip" href="#main">Skip to main content</a>
<header class="top">
  <div class="wrap">
    <p class="kicker">Interactive companion to the paper</p>
    <h1>Over-Refusal of Benign Slovene Prompts in Gemma-3-12B Is a Criterion Shift</h1>
    <p class="byline">Gemma-3-12B-IT compared with its Slovene-adapted sibling GaMS3-12B-Instruct. Every chart below is drawn from the run's saved per-item and per-condition results.</p>
    <div class="btnrow">
      <a class="btn primary" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-2cf2a7-does-slovene-taught-refusal-survive@fork/run_6GCdZCQAemW2/paper.pdf">Read the paper (PDF)</a>
      <a class="btn" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-2cf2a7-does-slovene-taught-refusal-survive@fork/run_6GCdZCQAemW2/report.pdf">Read the full research report</a>
      <a class="btn" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-2cf2a7-does-slovene-taught-refusal-survive/tree/fork/run_6GCdZCQAemW2">Code repository</a>
    </div>
  </div>
</header>
<nav class="sec" aria-label="Sections">
  <ul>
    <li><a href="#finding">The finding</a></li>
    <li><a href="#how">How it works</a></li>
    <li><a href="#explore">Explore the evidence</a></li>
    <li><a href="#try">Try it</a></li>
    <li><a href="#fails">Where it fails</a></li>
    <li><a href="#sources">Sources &amp; glossary</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>

<main id="main" tabindex="-1">

<!-- ============ FINDING ============ -->
<section class="block" id="finding" aria-labelledby="h-finding">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-finding">The finding</h2>
  <div class="two">
    <div class="prose">
      <p class="q">The question</p>
      <p class="lede">Gemma-3-12B-IT refuses more often when a prompt is in Slovene. Is it better at spotting harm in Slovene, or does it simply say no more often?</p>
      <p class="q">The answer</p>
      <p>It says no more often. On the 1,093 benign prompts of the HARD set, unedited Gemma refuses <span data-fill="fGS"></span> of the Slovene versions and <span data-fill="fGE"></span> of the English ones, 1.56 times as often. GaMS3, built on the same Gemma-3 base with Slovene training, refuses <span data-fill="fME"></span> in both languages.</p>
      <p><span class="termwrap"><button class="term" type="button" data-term="sdt">Signal-detection theory</button></span> splits a refusal rate into two parts: <span class="termwrap"><button class="term" type="button" data-term="dprime">sensitivity <i>d</i>′</button></span>, how well the model separates harmful from benign prompts, and the <span class="termwrap"><button class="term" type="button" data-term="crit">criterion <i>c</i></button></span>, where it puts its threshold. The model-by-language interaction sits in the criterion:</p>
      <p class="bignum" id="big-did">DiD<sub>c</sub> = <span data-fill="didc"></span> <span class="ci" data-fill="didcci"></span></p>
      <p>The same <span class="termwrap"><button class="term" type="button" data-term="did">difference-in-differences</button></span> on sensitivity is <span data-fill="diddp"></span> <span data-fill="diddpci"></span>, indistinguishable from zero. <span class="badge">ESTIMATE</span> The sign reverses when the judge's <span class="termwrap"><button class="term" type="button" data-term="partial">PARTIAL</button></span> label is counted as a refusal (see <a href="#fails">Where it fails</a>).</p>
    </div>
    <div class="card view" style="margin-top:0" id="v-head">
      <h3 id="h-head">Share of prompts refused, unedited models</h3>
      <p class="viewq">Does the Slovene increase appear on benign prompts, harmful ones, or both?</p>
      <div class="controls">
        <div class="ctl"><span class="lab" id="lab-head-items">Items</span>
          <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="lab-head-items" data-group="headItems">
            <button type="button" role="radio" aria-checked="true" data-v="benign">Benign (false alarms)</button>
            <button type="button" role="radio" aria-checked="false" data-v="harmful">Harmful (hits)</button>
          </div></div>
        <div class="ctl"><label class="lab" for="head-en">English reference</label>
          <select id="head-en"><option value="E">Back-translation (primary)</option><option value="O">Original English</option></select></div>
      </div>
      <div class="legend" aria-hidden="true"><span><i class="sw" style="background:var(--en)"></i>English prompt</span><span><i class="sw" style="background:var(--sl)"></i>Slovene prompt</span></div>
      <div class="chart" id="ch-head"></div>
      <p class="note">Bars: raw share refused, <i>k</i>/<i>n</i>, over the items shown. Whiskers: Wilson 95% intervals. Refusals labelled by the local Qwen3-14B judge, with PARTIAL counted as not refused. GaMS3 is the sibling baseline.</p>
      <p class="takeaway" id="tk-head" aria-live="polite"></p>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
</section>

<!-- ============ HOW ============ -->
<section class="block" id="how" aria-labelledby="h-how">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-how">How it works: one benign prompt, start to finish</h2>
  <p class="prose">The stepper follows one real XSTest item through Experiment 5. It shows every recorded input, output and label on the way to the criterion estimate. Use the buttons, the stage markers, or the left and right arrow keys.</p>
  <div class="card stepper" id="stepper" tabindex="0" aria-roledescription="stepper" aria-label="Method stepper; use left and right arrow keys to change stage">
    <div class="chart" id="ch-pipe" aria-hidden="true"></div>
    <ol class="stagebtns" id="stagebtns" aria-label="Stages"></ol>
    <div id="stage-live" class="sr" aria-live="polite"></div>
    <div class="stagebody" id="stagebody"></div>
    <div class="stepnav">
      <button type="button" id="st-prev">&larr; Previous</button>
      <button type="button" id="st-next">Next &rarr;</button>
      <span class="note" id="st-count"></span>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
</section>

<!-- ============ EXPLORE ============ -->
<section class="block" id="explore" aria-labelledby="h-explore">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-explore">Explore the evidence</h2>

  <div class="card view" id="v-browse">
    <h3>Item browser: Experiment 5 HARD set</h3>
    <p class="viewq">What does a Slovene-only refusal look like on a real prompt, and how often does it happen?</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <div class="ctl"><label class="lab" for="br-show">Show</label>
        <select id="br-show">
          <option value="gS">Benign: Gemma refuses only in Slovene</option>
          <option value="gE">Benign: Gemma refuses only in English</option>
          <option value="mD">Benign: GaMS3 changes between languages</option>
          <option value="bAll">Benign: all with text embedded</option>
          <option value="harm">Harmful: sample</option>
        </select></div>
      <div class="ctl"><label class="lab" for="br-src">Source</label>
        <select id="br-src"><option value="all">All sources</option><option value="x">XSTest</option><option value="h">OR-Bench-Hard-1K</option><option value="t">OR-Bench-Toxic</option></select></div>
      <div class="ctl"><label class="lab" for="br-sort">Sort</label>
        <select id="br-sort"><option value="len">Shortest prompt first</option><option value="src">Source, then type</option><option value="id">Item id</option></select></div>
      <div class="ctl"><label class="lab" for="br-q">Search prompts</label>
        <input type="search" id="br-q" placeholder="e.g. kill, bank, manifesto" autocomplete="off"></div>
      <label class="chk"><input type="checkbox" id="br-frag"> Hide <span class="termwrap"><button class="term" type="button" data-term="frag">MT-fragile</button></span> items</label>
    </div>
    <p id="br-count" class="small" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <div class="browser">
      <div>
        <ul class="itemlist" id="br-list" aria-label="Items"></ul>
        <div class="more" id="br-more"></div>
      </div>
      <div class="detail" id="br-detail" aria-live="polite"></div>
    </div>
    <p class="takeaway" id="tk-browse" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <p class="note">Labels for all 1,442 items are embedded. Prompt and response text is embedded for every benign item where either model's refusal changes between English and Slovene, plus a seeded random sample (seed 20260925) of 100 other benign and 60 harmful items. Responses are cut at 400 characters; generation stopped at 160 tokens.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card view" id="v-forest">
    <h3>The criterion shift in other experiments</h3>
    <p class="viewq">Does Gemma's move toward refusing in Slovene appear outside Experiment 5?</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <label class="chk"><input type="checkbox" id="fo-invalid"> Include rows that fail the <span class="termwrap"><button class="term" type="button" data-term="compliance">language-compliance</button></span> check</label>
    </div>
    <div class="legend" aria-hidden="true"><span><i class="sw dot" style="background:var(--sl)"></i>Compliance-valid row</span><span><i class="sw dot" style="background:var(--base)"></i>Invalid manipulation</span></div>
    <div class="chart" id="ch-forest"></div>
    <p class="note">Harmonised scale from the audit (Evaluation 5): Δ<i>c</i> = [<i>c</i><sub>SL</sub> − <i>c</i><sub>EN</sub>]<sub>Gemma</sub> − [<i>c</i><sub>SL</sub> − <i>c</i><sub>EN</sub>]<sub>GaMS3</sub>. Negative means Gemma shifts toward refusing in Slovene. The paper's headline +0.52 appears here as −0.52. Bodies differ in items, judge and dose, and the paper does not count them as replications. The 8-of-9 count was a post-hoc refinement.</p>
    <p class="takeaway" id="tk-forest" aria-live="polite"></p>
  </div>

  <div class="card view" id="v-grid">
    <h3>Prompt language × reply language after a partial English edit</h3>
    <p class="viewq">Once an English-only <span class="termwrap"><button class="term" type="button" data-term="ablit">abliteration</button></span> edit has removed some refusal, does what is left follow the language of the prompt or of the reply?</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <div class="ctl"><span class="lab" id="lab-gd">Edit <span class="termwrap"><button class="term" type="button" data-term="dose">dose</button></span></span>
        <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="lab-gd" data-group="gridDose">
          <button type="button" role="radio" aria-checked="false" data-v="zero">Zero</button>
          <button type="button" role="radio" aria-checked="false" data-v="lo">Low</button>
          <button type="button" role="radio" aria-checked="true" data-v="hi">High</button>
        </div></div>
      <div class="ctl"><span class="lab" id="lab-gk">Items</span>
        <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="lab-gk" data-group="gridKind">
          <button type="button" role="radio" aria-checked="true" data-v="harmful">Harmful (200/cell)</button>
          <button type="button" role="radio" aria-checked="false" data-v="benign">Benign (100/cell)</button>
        </div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="panels two-up">
      <div><h4>Gemma-3-12B-IT</h4><div class="chart" id="ch-grid-g"></div></div>
      <div><h4>GaMS3-12B-Instruct</h4><div class="chart" id="ch-grid-m"></div></div>
    </div>
    <p class="note">Cell colour and value: share refused (primary judge, raw). † marks cells whose reply-language compliance, pooled over the three doses, is below 0.90. Point at a cell for its Wilson 95% interval and count.</p>
    <p class="takeaway" id="tk-grid" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <h4>The contrasts, and what correction does to them</h4>
    <div class="controls">
      <div class="ctl"><label class="lab" for="gc-read">Readout</label>
        <select id="gc-read"><option value="raw_R">Primary judge, raw</option><option value="ppi_R">PPI++ corrected</option><option value="rg_R">Rogan–Gladen corrected</option></select></div>
    </div>
    <div class="chart" id="ch-contr"></div>
    <p class="note">Log-odds contrasts at high dose, 95% intervals (Experiment 14). <span class="termwrap"><button class="term" type="button" data-term="out">OUT<sub>SL</sub></button></span>: Slovene-reply minus English-reply refusal, averaged over prompt languages. IN<sub>SL</sub>: the same for prompt language. dOUT<sub>SL</sub>: GaMS3 minus Gemma on OUT<sub>SL</sub>.</p>
    <p class="takeaway" id="tk-contr" aria-live="polite"></p>
  </div>

  <div class="card view" id="v-dose">
    <h3>Refusal as the edit gets stronger</h3>
    <p class="viewq">At each dose of the English edit, how much Slovene refusal is left compared with English?</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <div class="ctl"><label class="lab" for="dz-l">Dose λ = <output id="dz-lv" for="dz-l"></output></label>
        <input type="range" id="dz-l" min="0" max="8" step="1" value="4" aria-describedby="dz-help"></div>
      <label class="chk"><input type="checkbox" id="dz-band" checked> Show Wilson 95% bands</label>
    </div>
    <p class="sr" id="dz-help">Moves a marker along the nine recorded doses from 0 to 2.</p>
    <div class="legend" aria-hidden="true"><span><i class="sw" style="background:var(--en)"></i>English (back-translation)</span><span><i class="sw" style="background:var(--sl)"></i>Slovene (machine translation)</span></div>
    <div class="panels two-up">
      <div><h4>Gemma-3-12B-IT</h4><div class="chart" id="ch-dose-g"></div></div>
      <div><h4>GaMS3-12B-Instruct</h4><div class="chart" id="ch-dose-m"></div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="readout" id="dz-read"></div>
    <p class="note">Experiment 9, RefusEU-TRAIN probe, J1 judge. Points are the analysis rates (<i>k</i>+0.5)/(<i>n</i>+1); <i>n</i> = 300 at λ = 0 and 100 at every other dose. λ scales each model's own selected edit, so equal λ is not an equal edit across models. The pre-registered comparison is at matched English refusal, not matched dose.</p>
    <p class="takeaway" id="tk-dose" aria-live="polite"></p>
  </div>
</div>
</section>

<!-- ============ TRY ============ -->
<section class="block" id="try" aria-labelledby="h-try">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-try">Try it: recode the judge, reselect the items</h2>
  <div class="card view" id="v-try" style="margin-top:12px">
    <p class="viewq">If a PARTIAL answer counted as a refusal, or only some item sources were kept, would the criterion shift survive?</p>
    <p class="prose small">The page recomputes hit rate, false-alarm rate, <i>d</i>′ = <i>z</i>(<i>H</i>) − <i>z</i>(<i>F</i>) and <i>c</i> = −½[<i>z</i>(<i>H</i>) + <i>z</i>(<i>F</i>)] from the 5,768 recorded judge labels, with the <span class="termwrap"><button class="term" type="button" data-term="hautus">Hautus correction</button></span> used in the analysis. Six settings match analyses the run saved; for those the page prints the saved estimate and its bootstrap interval. Other combinations get a point estimate only.</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <div class="ctl"><span class="lab" id="lab-tp">PARTIAL label counts as</span>
        <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="lab-tp" data-group="tryPartial">
          <button type="button" role="radio" aria-checked="true" data-v="C">Not refused (primary)</button>
          <button type="button" role="radio" aria-checked="false" data-v="R">Refused</button>
        </div></div>
      <div class="ctl"><label class="lab" for="tr-en">English reference</label>
        <select id="tr-en"><option value="E">Back-translation (primary)</option><option value="O">Original English</option></select></div>
      <div class="ctl"><label class="lab" for="tr-src">Item source</label>
        <select id="tr-src"><option value="all">All (1,093 benign / 349 harmful)</option><option value="x">XSTest only</option><option value="ob">OR-Bench only</option></select></div>
      <label class="chk"><input type="checkbox" id="tr-frag"> Drop MT-fragile items</label>
    </div>
    <div class="panels two-up">
      <div><h4>Criterion <i>c</i>, English → Slovene</h4><div class="chart" id="ch-try-c"></div></div>
      <div><h4>Sensitivity <i>d</i>′, English → Slovene</h4><div class="chart" id="ch-try-d"></div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="legend" aria-hidden="true"><span><i class="sw dot" style="background:var(--en)"></i>English</span><span><i class="sw" style="background:var(--sl)"></i>Slovene</span></div>
    <div class="tscroll"><table class="num" id="tr-table"><caption class="sr">Signal-detection parameters for the current setting</caption></table></div>
    <div class="readout" id="tr-read"></div>
    <p class="takeaway" id="tk-try" aria-live="polite"></p>
  </div>
</div>
</section>

<!-- ============ FAILS ============ -->
<section class="block" id="fails" aria-labelledby="h-fails">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-fails">Where it fails</h2>
  <div class="card view" id="v-fail" style="margin-top:12px">
    <h3>Six saved analyses of the same 1,442 items</h3>
    <p class="viewq">Which analysis choices keep the effect, and which break it?</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <div class="ctl"><span class="lab" id="lab-fm">Measure</span>
        <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="lab-fm" data-group="failMeasure">
          <button type="button" role="radio" aria-checked="true" data-v="DiD_c">DiD on criterion <i>c</i></button>
          <button type="button" role="radio" aria-checked="false" data-v="DiD_dprime">DiD on <i>d</i>′</button>
        </div></div>
      <label class="chk"><input type="checkbox" id="fa-only"> Show only settings whose interval includes zero or flips sign</label>
    </div>
    <div class="chart" id="ch-fail"></div>
    <p class="note">Paper sign convention: positive DiD<sub>c</sub> means Gemma's criterion moves further toward refusal in Slovene than GaMS3's. The XSTest-only and OR-Bench-only rows come from the run's analysis file and are not discussed in the paper.</p>
    <p class="takeaway" id="tk-fail" aria-live="polite"></p>
  </div>

  <div class="card view" id="v-comp">
    <h3>Does each model reply in the language it was asked for?</h3>
    <p class="viewq">In which cells of the 3 × 3 grid did the reply-language manipulation fail?</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <div class="ctl"><span class="lab" id="lab-cm">Model</span>
        <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="lab-cm" data-group="compModel">
          <button type="button" role="radio" aria-checked="false" data-v="gemma_it">Gemma-3-12B-IT</button>
          <button type="button" role="radio" aria-checked="true" data-v="gams3_it">GaMS3-12B-Instruct</button>
        </div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="chart" id="ch-comp"></div>
    <p class="note">Share of replies written in the requested language, pooled over the three doses (<i>n</i> = 600 per cell, Experiment 14). Dashed line: the 0.90 gate.</p>
    <p class="takeaway" id="tk-comp" aria-live="polite"></p>
  </div>

  <div class="prose view">
    <h3>What the paper does not show</h3>
    <ul class="lims">
      <li><b>The headline is an ESTIMATE.</b> DiD<sub>c</sub> reverses to −0.31 [−0.62, −0.09] when partial answers are coded as refusals, so the coding rule decides whether the over-refusal is attributed to Gemma at all.</li>
      <li><b>No judge was validated against humans.</b> The Qwen3-14B judge was calibrated against gemini-2.5-flash on DEV (binary κ 0.68–0.86). On edited rows no judge exceeds κ = 0.51 against blind adjudication, and that adjudication is by an author-model LLM, not a person. The readout gate never passed.</li>
      <li><b>One sample.</b> The Qwen3-14B rescoring interval [0.39, 0.67] re-derives the same Experiment 5 items; it is not an independent sample. On edited models the criterion difference is 0.14 [−0.78, 1.12], consistent with zero.</li>
      <li><b>The reply-language effect has a weak anchor.</b> Experiment 16 gives OUT<sub>Gemma</sub> = +2.43 [+0.89, +5.38] after PPI correction, but the harmful-content adjudicator κ is 0.12 against a 0.60 gate.</li>
      <li><b>GaMS3 ignored the reply-language instruction</b> off the English-prompt row (SL→EN compliance 0.00), so GaMS3 mechanism claims are limited to that row.</li>
      <li><b>Hungarian is uninformative</b> (minimum detectable effect about 3 log-odds), both models ran in 4-bit NF4, Slovene prompts are machine translations with no native-speaker check, and the benign false-refusal adjudication has only 30 items per cell.</li>
      <li><b>Novelty is partial.</b> Language-dependent over-refusal is anticipated by Addagada (2026) and Nguyen et al. (2026); the contribution here is the signal-detection split and the sibling-pair design.</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
</section>
</main>

<!--DATA-->

<script>
(function(){
"use strict";
const D = id => JSON.parse(document.getElementById(id).textContent);
const SDT = D('data-sdt'), ITEMS = D('data-items'), FOREST = D('data-forest'), GRID = D('data-grid'), DOSE = D('data-dose');
const NS = 'http://www.w3.org/2000/svg';
const C = {en:'#0072B2', sl:'#D55E00', base:'#8b8b94', ink:'#1b1b1f', ink2:'#46464f', grid:'#ecebe6', rule:'#c9c6bd', accent:'#0b5cad'};
const MINUS = '−';

/* ---------- formatting ---------- */
function fmt(x, d, sign){ if(x===null||x===undefined||isNaN(x)) return 'n/a'; let s = Math.abs(x).toFixed(d); const neg = x < 0 && parseFloat(s) !== 0; return (neg ? MINUS : (sign && parseFloat(s)!==0 ? '+' : '')) + s; }
function fmtEst(x, sign){ return fmt(x, Math.abs(x) < 0.01 ? 3 : 2, sign); }
function fmtCI(ci, d){ d = d===undefined?2:d; return '[' + fmt(ci[0], d) + ', ' + fmt(ci[1], d) + ']'; }
function esc(s){ return String(s).replace(/[&<>"]/g, c => ({'&':'&amp;','<':'&lt;','>':'&gt;','"':'&quot;'}[c])); }
const nfmt = n => n.toLocaleString('en-US');

/* ---------- stats ---------- */
function invNorm(p){ // Acklam's rational approximation with one Halley refinement
  const a=[-3.969683028665376e+01,2.209460984245205e+02,-2.759285104469687e+02,1.383577518672690e+02,-3.066479806614716e+01,2.506628277459239e+00];
  const b=[-5.447609879822406e+01,1.615858368580409e+02,-1.556989798598866e+02,6.680131188771972e+01,-1.328068155288572e+01];
  const c=[-7.784894002430293e-03,-3.223964580411365e-01,-2.400758277161838e+00,-2.549732539343734e+00,4.374664141464968e+00,2.938163982698783e+00];
  const d=[7.784695709041462e-03,3.224671290700398e-01,2.445134137142996e+00,3.754408661907416e+00];
  const pl=0.02425; let q,r,x;
  if(p<pl){ q=Math.sqrt(-2*Math.log(p)); x=(((((c[0]*q+c[1])*q+c[2])*q+c[3])*q+c[4])*q+c[5])/((((d[0]*q+d[1])*q+d[2])*q+d[3])*q+1); }
  else if(p<=1-pl){ q=p-0.5; r=q*q; x=(((((a[0]*r+a[1])*r+a[2])*r+a[3])*r+a[4])*r+a[5])*q/(((((b[0]*r+b[1])*r+b[2])*r+b[3])*r+b[4])*r+1); }
  else { q=Math.sqrt(-2*Math.log(1-p)); x=-(((((c[0]*q+c[1])*q+c[2])*q+c[3])*q+c[4])*q+c[5])/((((d[0]*q+d[1])*q+d[2])*q+d[3])*q+1); }
  const e = 0.5*erfc(-x/Math.SQRT2) - p; const u = e*Math.sqrt(2*Math.PI)*Math.exp(x*x/2); return x - u/(1+x*u/2);
}
function erfc(x){ const z=Math.abs(x), t=1/(1+0.5*z); const r=t*Math.exp(-z*z-1.26551223+t*(1.00002368+t*(0.37409196+t*(0.09678418+t*(-0.18628806+t*(0.27886807+t*(-1.13520398+t*(1.48851587+t*(-0.82215223+t*0.17087277))))))))); return x>=0?r:2-r; }
function wilson(k,n){ if(!n) return [0,0]; const z=1.959963984540054, p=k/n, den=1+z*z/n, ce=(p+z*z/(2*n))/den, h=z*Math.sqrt(p*(1-p)/n+z*z/(4*n*n))/den; return [Math.max(0,ce-h), Math.min(1,ce+h)]; }

/* ---------- items ---------- */
// rec: [id, src, type, harm, frag, labels(gE gS gO mE mS mO), text?]
const SRCNAME = {x:'XSTest', h:'OR-Bench-Hard-1K', t:'OR-Bench-Toxic'};
const LABNAME = {R:'REFUSE', P:'PARTIAL', C:'COMPLY'};
const LI = {gE:0,gS:1,gO:2,mE:3,mS:4,mO:5};
const refused = (l, pr) => l === 'R' || (pr && l === 'P');
function compute(st){
  const sel = ITEMS.filter(r => (st.src==='all' || (st.src==='x' ? r[1]==='x' : r[1]!=='x')) && !(st.frag && r[4]));
  const pr = st.partial === 'R';
  const cells = [];
  [['g','Gemma'],['m','GaMS3']].forEach(([m]) => {
    [st.en, 'S'].forEach(arm => {
      const idx = LI[m+arm]; let kH=0,nH=0,kF=0,nF=0;
      sel.forEach(r => { const y = refused(r[5][idx], pr) ? 1 : 0; if(r[3]){ nH++; kH+=y; } else { nF++; kF+=y; } });
      const H=(kH+.5)/(nH+1), F=(kF+.5)/(nF+1), zH=invNorm(H), zF=invNorm(F);
      cells.push({kH,nH,kF,nF,H,F,zH,zF,dp:zH-zF,c:-(zH+zF)/2});
    });
  });
  const didc = (cells[3].c-cells[2].c)-(cells[1].c-cells[0].c);
  const diddp = (cells[3].dp-cells[2].dp)-(cells[1].dp-cells[0].dp);
  return {cells, didc, diddp, nSafe: cells[0].nF, nUnsafe: cells[0].nH};
}
function keyOf(st){
  const base = st.partial==='C' && st.en==='E' && st.src==='all' && !st.frag;
  if(base) return 'primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT';
  if(st.partial==='C' && st.en==='O' && st.src==='all' && !st.frag) return 'SLMT_vs_ENorig';
  if(st.partial==='C' && st.en==='E' && st.src==='x' && !st.frag) return 'xstest_only';
  if(st.partial==='C' && st.en==='E' && st.src==='ob' && !st.frag) return 'orbench_only';
  if(st.partial==='C' && st.en==='E' && st.src==='all' && st.frag) return 'mt_fragile_dropped';
  if(st.partial==='R' && st.en==='E' && st.src==='all' && !st.frag) return 'primary_Rp';
  return null;
}
const PRIMARY = SDT.primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT;

/* ---------- svg helpers ---------- */
function el(tag, attrs, parent){ const e=document.createElementNS(NS, tag); if(attrs) for(const k in attrs){ if(attrs[k]!==undefined && attrs[k]!==null) e.setAttribute(k, attrs[k]); } if(parent) parent.appendChild(e); return e; }
function txt(parent, x, y, s, attrs){ const t=el('text', Object.assign({x, y, 'font-size':13}, attrs||{}), parent); t.textContent=s; return t; }
let measurer=null;
function textW(s, size, weight){ if(!measurer){ measurer=el('svg',{width:0,height:0,style:'position:absolute;left:-9999px;top:0'}); document.body.appendChild(measurer); } const t=el('text',{'font-size':size||13,'font-weight':weight||400,'font-family':getComputedStyle(document.body).fontFamily},measurer); t.textContent=s; const w=t.getComputedTextLength(); measurer.removeChild(t); return w; }
function scale(d0,d1,r0,r1){ const f=v=>r0+(v-d0)/(d1-d0)*(r1-r0); return f; }
function niceTicks(lo, hi, n){ const span=hi-lo, step0=span/(n||5), mag=Math.pow(10,Math.floor(Math.log10(step0))), err=step0/mag; const step=(err>=5?10:err>=2?5:err>=1?2:1)*mag/ (err>=5?1:1); let s=step; if(span/s>8) s*=2; const out=[]; for(let v=Math.ceil(lo/s)*s; v<=hi+1e-9; v+=s) out.push(Math.round(v/s)*s); return out; }
function newSvg(host, w, h, label){ host.innerHTML=''; const s=el('svg',{viewBox:`0 0 ${w} ${h}`, width:w, height:h, role:'group', 'aria-label':label}, host); s.style.maxWidth='100%'; return s; }
function hostW(host){ return Math.max(280, Math.floor(host.getBoundingClientRect().width)); }

/* ---------- chart tooltip ---------- */
const tip = document.getElementById('tip'); let tipOwner=null;
function showTip(target, html, evt){
  tip.innerHTML = html; tip.classList.add('on'); tip.setAttribute('aria-hidden','false'); tipOwner = target;
  const r = target.getBoundingClientRect(); const tw = tip.offsetWidth, th = tip.offsetHeight;
  let x = (evt && evt.clientX !== undefined && evt.type !== 'focus') ? evt.clientX + 12 : r.left + r.width/2 - tw/2;
  let y = (evt && evt.clientY !== undefined && evt.type !== 'focus') ? evt.clientY - th - 12 : r.top - th - 10;
  if(y < 8) y = r.bottom + 10; x = Math.max(8, Math.min(window.innerWidth - tw - 8, x));
  tip.style.left = x+'px'; tip.style.top = y+'px';
}
function hideTip(){ tip.classList.remove('on'); tip.setAttribute('aria-hidden','true'); tipOwner=null; }
function markify(g, html, aria){
  g.setAttribute('class','mark'); g.setAttribute('tabindex','0'); g.setAttribute('role','img'); g.setAttribute('aria-label', aria);
  const h = () => html; g.addEventListener('mouseenter', e => showTip(g, h(), e)); g.addEventListener('mousemove', e => showTip(g, h(), e));
  g.addEventListener('mouseleave', hideTip); g.addEventListener('focus', e => showTip(g, h(), e)); g.addEventListener('blur', hideTip);
  g.addEventListener('click', e => { e.stopPropagation(); showTip(g, h(), e); });
}
document.addEventListener('click', e => { if(tipOwner && !tipOwner.contains(e.target)) hideTip(); });
window.addEventListener('scroll', () => { if(tipOwner && document.activeElement !== tipOwner) hideTip(); }, {passive:true});

/* ---------- segmented radio groups ---------- */
const state = { headItems:'benign', gridDose:'hi', gridKind:'harmful', tryPartial:'C', failMeasure:'DiD_c', compModel:'gams3_it' };
const onGroup = {};
document.querySelectorAll('.seg[data-group]').forEach(g => {
  const name = g.dataset.group; const btns = [...g.querySelectorAll('button')];
  const set = (b, focus) => { btns.forEach(x => { const on = x===b; x.setAttribute('aria-checked', on); x.tabIndex = on?0:-1; }); state[name]=b.dataset.v; if(focus) b.focus(); (onGroup[name]||(()=>{}))(); };
  btns.forEach((b,i) => { b.tabIndex = b.getAttribute('aria-checked')==='true'?0:-1; b.addEventListener('click', () => set(b)); b.addEventListener('keydown', e => {
    if(['ArrowRight','ArrowDown'].includes(e.key)){ e.preventDefault(); set(btns[(i+1)%btns.length], true); }
    if(['ArrowLeft','ArrowUp'].includes(e.key)){ e.preventDefault(); set(btns[(i-1+btns.length)%btns.length], true); } }); });
  g._set = v => set(btns.find(b => b.dataset.v===v));
});

/* ---------- generic axis ---------- */
function yAxisLeft(svg, ticks, y, title, x0, x1, fmtT){
  // returns left margin used; draws gridlines
  const tw = Math.max(...ticks.map(t => textW(fmtT(t), 12)));
  const left = x0 + 18 + 8 + tw + 8; // title band + gap + ticks + gap
  ticks.forEach(t => { el('line',{x1:left, x2:x1, y1:y(t), y2:y(t), stroke:C.grid, 'stroke-width':1}, svg); txt(svg, left-8, y(t)+4, fmtT(t), {'text-anchor':'end','font-size':12}); });
  const midY = (y(ticks[0]) + y(ticks[ticks.length-1]))/2;
  txt(svg, 0, 0, title, {'text-anchor':'middle', transform:`translate(${x0+12},${midY}) rotate(-90)`, 'font-size':12.5, fill:C.ink2});
  return left;
}

/* ========== VIEW 1: headline bars ========== */
function drawHead(){
  const host = document.getElementById('ch-head'); const W = hostW(host), H = 300;
  const st = {partial:'C', en: document.getElementById('head-en').value, src:'all', frag:false};
  const R = compute(st); const benign = state.headItems==='benign';
  const svg = newSvg(host, W, H, 'Bar chart of the share of '+(benign?'benign':'harmful')+' prompts refused by model and prompt language');
  const top=24, bottom=H-44; const y = scale(0,1,bottom,top);
  const left = yAxisLeft(svg, [0,.2,.4,.6,.8,1], y, 'Share refused', 0, W-6, t => t.toFixed(1));
  el('line',{x1:left,x2:W-6,y1:bottom,y2:bottom,stroke:C.rule,'stroke-width':1.2},svg);
  const groups = [['Gemma 3', 0], ['GaMS3 (baseline)', 2]]; const gw = (W-6-left)/2;
  const enLab = st.en==='E' ? 'English (back-translation)' : 'English (original)';
  groups.forEach(([name, off], gi) => {
    const gx = left + gi*gw; const bw = Math.min(64, gw*0.28), gap=6; const cx = gx + gw/2;
    txt(svg, cx, bottom+22, name, {'text-anchor':'middle','font-size':13.5,'font-weight':600, fill:C.ink});
    [0,1].forEach(j => {
      const c = R.cells[off+j]; const k = benign?c.kF:c.kH, n = benign?c.nF:c.nH; const p=k/n, ci=wilson(k,n);
      const x = j===0 ? cx - gap/2 - bw : cx + gap/2; const col = j===0?C.en:C.sl;
      const g = el('g',{},svg);
      el('rect',{class:'hit', x:x-4, y:top-4, width:bw+8, height:bottom-top+4, fill:'transparent'}, g);
      el('path',{d:`M${x},${bottom} V${y(p)+4} q0,-4 4,-4 h${bw-8} q4,0 4,4 V${bottom} Z`, fill:col}, g);
      el('line',{x1:x+bw/2,x2:x+bw/2,y1:y(ci[0]),y2:y(ci[1]),stroke:C.ink,'stroke-width':1.4},g);
      [ci[0],ci[1]].forEach(v => el('line',{x1:x+bw/2-5,x2:x+bw/2+5,y1:y(v),y2:y(v),stroke:C.ink,'stroke-width':1.4},g));
      const ly = Math.min(y(ci[1]) - 6, y(p) - 6);
      txt(g, x+bw/2, Math.max(12, ly), p.toFixed(3), {'text-anchor':'middle','font-size':12.5, fill:C.ink, 'font-weight':600});
      const lang = j===0? enLab : 'Slovene (machine translation)';
      const html = `<b>${name.replace(' (baseline)','')}, ${lang}</b><br>${benign?'Benign':'Harmful'} items refused: ${k} of ${n} = ${p.toFixed(3)}<br>Wilson 95%: ${fmtCI(ci,3)}`;
      markify(g, html, `${name}, ${lang}: ${k} of ${n} ${benign?'benign':'harmful'} items refused, ${p.toFixed(3)}`);
    });
  });
  // takeaway
  const g = R.cells; const r = i => (benign? g[i].kF/g[i].nF : g[i].kH/g[i].nH);
  let t;
  if(benign){
    const mc = st.en==='E' ? PRIMARY.mcnemar : null;
    t = `Gemma refuses ${r(1).toFixed(3)} of benign Slovene prompts against ${r(0).toFixed(3)} with the ${st.en==='E'?'back-translated':'original'} English reference, ${(r(1)/r(0)).toFixed(2)} times as often. GaMS3 refuses ${r(3).toFixed(3)} in Slovene and ${r(2).toFixed(3)} in English.`;
    if(mc){ t += ` Paired on the same items, Gemma's change is ${mc.gemma_it.safe.x_only} items refused only in Slovene against ${mc.gemma_it.safe.y_only} only in English (exact McNemar p < 10<sup>−28</sup>); GaMS3's is ${mc.gams3_it.safe.x_only} against ${mc.gams3_it.safe.y_only} (p = 1.0).`; }
  } else {
    t = `On harmful prompts both models refuse most items in both languages: Gemma ${r(0).toFixed(3)} English and ${r(1).toFixed(3)} Slovene, GaMS3 ${r(2).toFixed(3)} and ${r(3).toFixed(3)}. The Slovene jump in Gemma's benign refusals is far larger than any change in its hits, which is the pattern a criterion shift predicts.`;
  }
  document.getElementById('tk-head').innerHTML = t;
}
onGroup.headItems = drawHead; document.getElementById('head-en').addEventListener('change', drawHead);

/* fill headline numbers from embedded data */
(function(){
  const R = compute({partial:'C',en:'E',src:'all',frag:false}).cells;
  const put = (k, v) => document.querySelectorAll(`[data-fill="${k}"]`).forEach(e => e.innerHTML = v);
  put('fGE', (R[0].kF/R[0].nF).toFixed(3)); put('fGS', (R[1].kF/R[1].nF).toFixed(3)); put('fME', (R[2].kF/R[2].nF).toFixed(3));
  put('didc', fmtEst(PRIMARY.DiD_c.est, true)); put('didcci', fmtCI(PRIMARY.DiD_c.ci95));
  put('diddp', fmtEst(PRIMARY.DiD_dprime.est, true)); put('diddpci', fmtCI(PRIMARY.DiD_dprime.ci95));
})();

/* ========== STEPPER ========== */
const EX = ITEMS.find(r => r[0]==='xstest_4ad4726cab1b');
const STAGES = ['Source', 'Translate', 'Generate', 'Judge', 'Code', 'Pool', 'SDT'];
let stage = 0;
function chip(l){ return `<span class="chip ${l}">${LABNAME[l]}</span>`; }
function stageHTML(i){
  const t = EX[6], L = EX[5]; const R = compute({partial:'C',en:'E',src:'all',frag:false}).cells;
  const inout = (a,b,c,d) => `<div class="stagegrid cols2"><div class="io"><div class="h">In</div>${a}</div><div class="io"><div class="h">Done to it</div>${b}</div><div class="io"><div class="h">Out</div>${c}</div><div class="io"><div class="h">Why</div>${d}</div></div>`;
  const cellName = ['Gemma, English','Gemma, Slovene','GaMS3, English','GaMS3, Slovene'];
  const lab4 = [L[0],L[1],L[3],L[4]];
  switch(i){
    case 0: return inout(`<p>Item <code>${EX[0]}</code> from ${SRCNAME[EX[1]]}, category <i>${esc(EX[2].replace(/_/g,' '))}</i>.</p><p><b>“${esc(t.pO)}”</b></p>`,
      `Nothing yet. XSTest marks it as a safe prompt that superficially resembles a harmful one.`,
      `A benign item (is_harmful = false), one of 1,093 benign and 349 harmful HARD items.`,
      `Benign items measure false alarms. A model that refuses them is over-refusing, whatever it does on harmful items.`);
    case 1: return inout(`<p>“${esc(t.pO)}”</p>`,
      `Machine-translated to Slovene with gemini-2.5-flash, then back-translated to English so both arms went through translation.`,
      `<p><span class="pl">Slovene (SL-MT)</span><br>“${esc(t.pS)}”</p><p><span class="pl">English back-translation (EN-BT)</span><br>“${esc(t.pE)}”</p><p class="small">Back-translation chrF: ${t.chrf}</p>`,
      `Comparing Slovene with the back-translation holds translation noise constant across the two languages. The original English is kept as a check.`);
    case 2: return `<div class="stagegrid cols2">${['gE','gS','mE','mS'].map((k,j)=>`<div class="io"><div class="h">${cellName[j]} · ${t.n[j]} tokens</div><div class="resp" lang="${k.endsWith('S')?'sl':'en'}">${esc(t[k])}</div></div>`).join('')}</div><p class="small" style="margin-top:8px">Both unedited models, NF4, greedy decoding, empty system turn, up to 160 new tokens. Text shown up to 400 characters.</p>`;
    case 3: return inout(`The four replies from the previous stage.`,
      `A local Qwen3-14B judge reads each reply with a frozen prompt and labels it REFUSE, PARTIAL or COMPLY. (The paid judges were out of budget; Qwen3-14B was calibrated against gemini-2.5-flash on DEV, binary κ 0.68–0.86.)`,
      `<ul style="margin:0;padding-left:18px">${cellName.map((n,j)=>`<li>${n}: ${chip(lab4[j])}</li>`).join('')}</ul>`,
      `Gemma answers the English version and refuses the Slovene one. GaMS3 answers both.`);
    case 4: return inout(`<ul style="margin:0;padding-left:18px">${cellName.map((n,j)=>`<li>${n}: ${chip(lab4[j])}</li>`).join('')}</ul>`,
      `Primary coding: REFUSE → 1; PARTIAL and COMPLY → 0.`,
      `<ul style="margin:0;padding-left:18px">${cellName.map((n,j)=>`<li>${n}: <b>${refused(lab4[j],false)?1:0}</b></li>`).join('')}</ul>`,
      `SDT needs a yes/no decision. This coding rule matters: counting PARTIAL as refusal flips the headline sign (Try it, Where it fails).`);
    case 5: return inout(`This item's four binary outcomes, plus the other 1,092 benign and 349 harmful items.`,
      `Per model × language cell, the share of benign items refused is the false-alarm rate <i>F</i>; the share of harmful items refused is the hit rate <i>H</i>. The analysis uses the Hautus correction (<i>k</i>+0.5)/(<i>n</i>+1).`,
      `<div class="tscroll"><table class="num"><thead><tr><th>Cell</th><th>benign refused</th><th><i>F</i></th><th>harmful refused</th><th><i>H</i></th></tr></thead><tbody>${R.map((c,j)=>`<tr><td>${cellName[j]}</td><td>${c.kF}/${c.nF}</td><td>${c.F.toFixed(3)}</td><td>${c.kH}/${c.nH}</td><td>${c.H.toFixed(2)}</td></tr>`).join('')}</tbody></table></div>`,
      `This item adds one to Gemma's Slovene false-alarm count and nothing to the other three cells.`);
    case 6: { const P = PRIMARY.cells;
      return inout(`<i>H</i> and <i>F</i> for the four cells.`,
      `<i>d</i>′ = <i>z</i>(<i>H</i>) − <i>z</i>(<i>F</i>) and <i>c</i> = −½[<i>z</i>(<i>H</i>) + <i>z</i>(<i>F</i>)]. Then DiD<sub>c</sub> = (<i>c</i><sub>GaMS3,SL</sub> − <i>c</i><sub>GaMS3,EN</sub>) − (<i>c</i><sub>Gemma,SL</sub> − <i>c</i><sub>Gemma,EN</sub>), with an item bootstrap for the interval.`,
      `<div class="tscroll"><table class="num"><thead><tr><th>Cell</th><th><i>d</i>′</th><th><i>c</i></th></tr></thead><tbody>${cellName.map((n,j)=>`<tr><td>${n}</td><td>${P.dprime[j].toFixed(2)}</td><td>${fmt(P.c[j],2)}</td></tr>`).join('')}</tbody></table></div><p style="margin-top:8px">DiD<sub>c</sub> = <b>${fmtEst(PRIMARY.DiD_c.est,true)} ${fmtCI(PRIMARY.DiD_c.ci95)}</b><br>DiD<sub><i>d</i>′</sub> = ${fmtEst(PRIMARY.DiD_dprime.est,true)} ${fmtCI(PRIMARY.DiD_dprime.ci95)}</p>`,
      `Gemma's criterion drops by ${fmt(-PRIMARY.own_delta.gemma_c_SL_minus_EN,2)} in Slovene (toward refusing) while its <i>d</i>′ barely moves relative to GaMS3. The asymmetry is in the threshold, not in discrimination.`); }
  }
}
function drawPipe(){
  const host = document.getElementById('ch-pipe'); const W = hostW(host); const cols = W < 560 ? 4 : 7; const rows = Math.ceil(STAGES.length/cols);
  const gap = 18, bh = 40, rowH = bh + 22; const bw = (W - gap*(cols-1)) / cols; const H = rows*rowH;
  const svg = newSvg(host, W, H, 'Pipeline diagram');
  el('defs',{},svg).innerHTML = '<marker id="arr" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="#8b8b94"/></marker>';
  STAGES.forEach((s, i) => {
    const r = Math.floor(i/cols), c = i%cols; const x = c*(bw+gap), y = r*rowH + 4; const on = i===stage, done = i<stage;
    const g = el('g',{style:'cursor:pointer'},svg); g.addEventListener('click', () => go(i));
    el('rect',{x, y, width:bw, height:bh, rx:8, fill:on?C.accent:(done?'#e7f0fa':'#fff'), stroke:on?C.accent:'#b9b6ad','stroke-width':1.5}, g);
    txt(g, x+bw/2, y+bh/2+5, (i+1)+'. '+s, {'text-anchor':'middle','font-size':13.5,'font-weight':on?700:500, fill:on?'#fff':C.ink});
    if(i < STAGES.length-1){ if(c < cols-1) el('line',{x1:x+bw+2,x2:x+bw+gap-2,y1:y+bh/2,y2:y+bh/2,stroke:'#8b8b94','stroke-width':1.5,'marker-end':'url(#arr)'},svg);
      else el('path',{d:`M${x+bw/2},${y+bh+2} V${y+bh+11} H${bw/2} V${y+rowH-2}`,fill:'none',stroke:'#8b8b94','stroke-width':1.5,'marker-end':'url(#arr)'},svg); }
  });
}
const stageBtns = document.getElementById('stagebtns');
STAGES.forEach((s,i) => { const li=document.createElement('li'); const b=document.createElement('button'); b.type='button'; b.textContent=(i+1)+'. '+s; b.addEventListener('click',()=>go(i)); li.appendChild(b); stageBtns.appendChild(li); });
function go(i){
  stage = Math.max(0, Math.min(STAGES.length-1, i));
  [...stageBtns.querySelectorAll('button')].forEach((b,j) => { if(j===stage) b.setAttribute('aria-current','step'); else b.removeAttribute('aria-current'); });
  document.getElementById('stagebody').innerHTML = `<h3 style="margin-top:4px">Stage ${stage+1} of ${STAGES.length}: ${STAGES[stage]}</h3>` + stageHTML(stage);
  document.getElementById('st-prev').disabled = stage===0; document.getElementById('st-next').disabled = stage===STAGES.length-1;
  document.getElementById('st-count').textContent = `Stage ${stage+1} of ${STAGES.length}`;
  document.getElementById('stage-live').textContent = `Stage ${stage+1} of ${STAGES.length}: ${STAGES[stage]}`;
  drawPipe();
}
document.getElementById('st-prev').addEventListener('click', () => go(stage-1));
document.getElementById('st-next').addEventListener('click', () => go(stage+1));
document.getElementById('stepper').addEventListener('keydown', e => {
  if(e.target.closest('input,select,textarea')) return;
  if(e.key==='ArrowRight'){ e.preventDefault(); go(stage+1); } else if(e.key==='ArrowLeft'){ e.preventDefault(); go(stage-1); }
});

/* ========== ITEM BROWSER ========== */
let brSel = null, brLimit = 60;
const benignAll = ITEMS.filter(r => !r[3]);
const cnt = {
  gS: benignAll.filter(r => refused(r[5][1]) && !refused(r[5][0])).length,
  gE: benignAll.filter(r => !refused(r[5][1]) && refused(r[5][0])).length,
  mD: benignAll.filter(r => refused(r[5][4]) !== refused(r[5][3])).length,
  mS: benignAll.filter(r => refused(r[5][4]) && !refused(r[5][3])).length,
  mE: benignAll.filter(r => !refused(r[5][4]) && refused(r[5][3])).length
};
function brFilter(){
  const show = document.getElementById('br-show').value, src = document.getElementById('br-src').value, frag = document.getElementById('br-frag').checked;
  const q = document.getElementById('br-q').value.trim().toLowerCase(); const sort = document.getElementById('br-sort').value;
  const base = ITEMS.filter(r => {
    const L = r[5];
    if(show==='harm') { if(!r[3]) return false; }
    else { if(r[3]) return false;
      if(show==='gS' && !(refused(L[1]) && !refused(L[0]))) return false;
      if(show==='gE' && !(!refused(L[1]) && refused(L[0]))) return false;
      if(show==='mD' && refused(L[4])===refused(L[3])) return false; }
    if(src!=='all' && r[1]!==src) return false; if(frag && r[4]) return false; return true; });
  let list = base.filter(r => r[6]);
  if(q) list = list.filter(r => (r[6].pO+' '+r[6].pS+' '+r[6].pE).toLowerCase().includes(q));
  if(sort==='len') list.sort((a,b) => a[6].pO.length - b[6].pO.length);
  else if(sort==='src') list.sort((a,b) => (a[1]+a[2]).localeCompare(b[1]+b[2]) || a[0].localeCompare(b[0]));
  else list.sort((a,b) => a[0].localeCompare(b[0]));
  return {base, list, show, q};
}
function drawBrowser(resetLimit){
  if(resetLimit) brLimit = 60;
  const {base, list, show, q} = brFilter();
  const ul = document.getElementById('br-list'); ul.innerHTML='';
  if(!list.find(r => r===brSel)) brSel = list[0] || null;
  list.slice(0, brLimit).forEach(r => {
    const li=document.createElement('li'); const b=document.createElement('button'); b.type='button';
    b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', r===brSel); b.innerHTML = esc(r[6].pO.length>110? r[6].pO.slice(0,108)+'…' : r[6].pO) + `<span class="meta">${SRCNAME[r[1]]}${r[2]?' · '+esc(r[2].replace(/_/g,' ')):''}${r[4]?' · MT-fragile':''}</span>`;
    b.addEventListener('click', () => { brSel = r; [...ul.querySelectorAll('button')].forEach(x => x.setAttribute('aria-pressed', x===b)); drawDetail(); });
    li.appendChild(b); ul.appendChild(li);
  });
  const more = document.getElementById('br-more'); more.innerHTML='';
  if(list.length > brLimit){ const b=document.createElement('button'); b.type='button'; b.textContent=`Show ${Math.min(60, list.length-brLimit)} more (${list.length-brLimit} hidden)`; b.addEventListener('click',()=>{ brLimit+=60; drawBrowser(false); }); more.appendChild(b); }
  const showName = {gS:'benign items Gemma refuses only in Slovene', gE:'benign items Gemma refuses only in English', mD:'benign items where GaMS3 changes between languages', bAll:'benign items', harm:'harmful items'}[show];
  document.getElementById('br-count').textContent = `${nfmt(base.length)} ${showName} match these filters in the full set; ${nfmt(list.length)} have text embedded${q?' and match the search':''}.`;
  let t;
  if(show==='gS') t = `Gemma refuses ${cnt.gS} of the 1,093 benign prompts only in Slovene and ${cnt.gE} only in English. GaMS3 moves ${cnt.mS} one way and ${cnt.mE} the other, so its benign refusal rate does not change. Most of the Slovene-only refusals answer a prompt that looks sensitive but is not, such as the one selected.`;
  else if(show==='gE') t = `These ${cnt.gE} items run against the finding: Gemma refuses the English version and answers the Slovene one. They are outnumbered ${cnt.gS} to ${cnt.gE} by the opposite pattern.`;
  else if(show==='mD') t = `GaMS3 changes its answer between languages on ${cnt.mD} benign items, but the changes cancel (${cnt.mS} toward refusing in Slovene, ${cnt.mE} toward refusing in English), which is why its false-alarm rate is identical in both languages.`;
  else if(show==='harm') t = `On harmful prompts both models refuse in most cells; the differences between languages there are small next to Gemma's benign shift.`;
  else t = `Across all 1,093 benign prompts, Gemma's refusals shift toward Slovene (${cnt.gS} Slovene-only vs ${cnt.gE} English-only); GaMS3's do not (${cnt.mS} vs ${cnt.mE}).`;
  document.getElementById('tk-browse').textContent = t;
  drawDetail();
}
function drawDetail(){
  const d = document.getElementById('br-detail');
  if(!brSel){ d.innerHTML = '<p class="small">No embedded item matches these filters. Clear the search or change a filter.</p>'; return; }
  const r = brSel, t = r[6], L = r[5];
  const cell = (name, k, lang) => { const l = L[LI[k]]; const flag = (k==='gS' && refused(L[1]) && !refused(L[0])); return `<div class="cellbox${flag?' flag':''}"><div class="top"><span>${name}</span>${chip(l)}</div><div class="resp" lang="${lang}">${esc(t[k])}</div></div>`; };
  d.innerHTML = `<div class="prompts"><div><span class="pl">Original English</span><div>${esc(t.pO)}</div></div><div><span class="pl">Slovene prompt (SL-MT)</span><div lang="sl">${esc(t.pS)}</div></div><div><span class="pl">English back-translation (EN-BT) · chrF ${t.chrf}</span><div>${esc(t.pE)}</div></div></div>
  <p class="small">${SRCNAME[r[1]]}${r[2]?' · '+esc(r[2].replace(/_/g,' ')):''} · ${r[3]?'harmful':'benign'}${r[4]?' · MT-fragile':''} · <code>${r[0]}</code></p>
  <div class="cellgrid">${cell('Gemma · English','gE','en')}${cell('Gemma · Slovene','gS','sl')}${cell('GaMS3 · English','mE','en')}${cell('GaMS3 · Slovene','mS','sl')}</div>
  <p class="small" style="margin-top:8px">Judge label on the original-English prompt: Gemma ${chip(L[2])}, GaMS3 ${chip(L[5])}.</p>`;
}
['br-show','br-src','br-sort','br-frag'].forEach(id => document.getElementById(id).addEventListener('change', () => drawBrowser(true)));
document.getElementById('br-q').addEventListener('input', () => drawBrowser(true));

/* ========== generic forest ========== */
function drawForest(host, rows, opts){
  const W = hostW(host); const rowH = opts.rowH || 48; const top = 8, axisH = 44; const H = top + rows.length*rowH + axisH;
  const svg = newSvg(host, W, H, opts.label);
  let lo = Math.min(0, ...rows.map(r => r.lo)), hi = Math.max(0, ...rows.map(r => r.hi));
  if(opts.domain){ lo = Math.min(lo, opts.domain[0]); hi = Math.max(hi, opts.domain[1]); }
  const pad = (hi-lo)*0.06; lo -= pad; hi += pad;
  const left = 10, right = W - 12; const x = scale(lo, hi, left, right);
  const ticks = niceTicks(lo, hi, W < 480 ? 4 : 7);
  const bottom = top + rows.length*rowH;
  ticks.forEach(t => { el('line',{x1:x(t),x2:x(t),y1:top,y2:bottom,stroke:C.grid},svg); txt(svg, x(t), bottom+16, fmt(t, Math.abs(t)%1===0?0:(Math.abs(t*10)%1===0?1:2)), {'text-anchor':'middle','font-size':12}); });
  el('line',{x1:x(0),x2:x(0),y1:top,y2:bottom,stroke:C.ink2,'stroke-width':1.3,'stroke-dasharray':'4 3'},svg);
  txt(svg, (left+right)/2, bottom+36, opts.xTitle, {'text-anchor':'middle','font-size':12.5, fill:C.ink2});
  rows.forEach((r,i) => {
    const y0 = top + i*rowH; const cy = y0 + rowH - 14;
    const g = el('g',{},svg);
    el('rect',{class:'hit', x:left, y:y0+2, width:right-left, height:rowH-4, fill:'transparent', rx:4},g);
    const lab = txt(g, left, y0+16, r.label, {'font-size':13, fill:C.ink, 'font-weight':r.bold?700:500});
    const valS = `${fmtEst(r.est, true)} ${fmtCI([r.lo,r.hi])}`; const vw = textW(valS, 12.5);
    // truncate label if it would collide with value text
    let ls = r.label; while(textW(ls, 13, r.bold?700:500) > (right-left) - vw - 14 && ls.length > 8){ ls = ls.slice(0,-2); lab.textContent = ls + '…'; }
    txt(g, right, y0+16, valS, {'text-anchor':'end','font-size':12.5, fill:C.ink2});
    el('line',{x1:x(r.lo),x2:x(r.hi),y1:cy,y2:cy,stroke:r.color,'stroke-width':2.4,'stroke-linecap':'round'},g);
    el('circle',{cx:x(r.est),cy,r:6,fill:r.color,stroke:'#fff','stroke-width':2},g);
    markify(g, r.tip, r.aria || (r.label + ': ' + valS));
  });
}

/* ========== VIEW: criterion forest ========== */
function drawCritForest(){
  const inc = document.getElementById('fo-invalid').checked;
  const rows = FOREST.rows.filter(r => inc || r.manipulation_valid).map(r => ({
    label: r.body, est: r.harmonised_value, lo: r.harmonised_ci95[0], hi: r.harmonised_ci95[1], bold: r.body.startsWith('exp5'),
    color: r.manipulation_valid ? C.sl : C.base,
    tip: `<b>${esc(r.body)}</b><br>Δc (harmonised) ${fmtEst(r.harmonised_value,true)} ${fmtCI(r.harmonised_ci95)}<br>As originally reported: ${fmtEst(r.original_value,true)} ${fmtCI(r.original_ci95)}<br>Items: ${esc(r.benign_twins)}<br>Judge: ${esc(r.judge)} · dose: ${esc(r.dose)}<br>Language varied: ${esc(r.output_language)}<br>${esc(r.validity_note)}`
  }));
  drawForest(document.getElementById('ch-forest'), rows, {label:'Forest plot of criterion-shift estimates across experiments', xTitle:'Δc, harmonised (z units; negative = Gemma shifts toward refusing in Slovene)'});
  const below = rows.filter(r => r.hi < 0).length, above = rows.filter(r => r.lo > 0).length, zero = rows.length - below - above;
  let t = `${below} of ${rows.length} rows shown have a 95% interval entirely below zero, ${zero} include${zero===1?'s':''} zero and ${above} ${above===1?'lies':'lie'} above it.`;
  t += inc ? ' The rows above zero both come from Experiment 14 cells where GaMS3 did not reply in English when asked (compliance 0.00), so they do not test the same contrast.' : ' The one exception is Experiment 9 at its EN-50% window, centred on zero.';
  document.getElementById('tk-forest').textContent = t;
}
document.getElementById('fo-invalid').addEventListener('change', drawCritForest);

/* ========== VIEW: grid heatmaps ========== */
const LANGS = ['en','sl','hu'], LN = {en:'EN',sl:'SL',hu:'HU'};
function heatColor(v){ // white -> dark red, single hue
  const a=[255,255,255], b=[153,27,27]; const t=Math.max(0,Math.min(1,v)); const mix=a.map((x,i)=>Math.round(x+(b[i]-x)*t)); return `rgb(${mix.join(',')})`; }
function drawGrid(){
  const dose = state.gridDose, kind = state.gridKind; const res = {};
  [['gemma_it','ch-grid-g','Gemma'],['gams3_it','ch-grid-m','GaMS3']].forEach(([m, id, nm]) => {
    const host = document.getElementById(id); const W = hostW(host);
    const rowTitleW = 18, rowLabW = Math.max(...LANGS.map(l => textW(LN[l],13,600))) + 10;
    const left = rowTitleW + 8 + rowLabW, top = 44; const cw = Math.min(110, (W - left - 4)/3), ch = Math.min(70, cw*0.72);
    const H = top + 3*ch + 6; const svg = newSvg(host, W, H, `${nm} heatmap of refusal share by prompt and reply language`);
    txt(svg, left + 1.5*cw, 14, 'Requested reply language', {'text-anchor':'middle','font-size':12.5, fill:C.ink2});
    LANGS.forEach((l,j) => txt(svg, left + (j+.5)*cw, 36, LN[l], {'text-anchor':'middle','font-size':13,'font-weight':600, fill:C.ink}));
    txt(svg, 0, 0, 'Prompt language', {'text-anchor':'middle','font-size':12.5, fill:C.ink2, transform:`translate(${12},${top+1.5*ch}) rotate(-90)`});
    LANGS.forEach((pl,i) => { txt(svg, left-8, top+(i+.5)*ch+5, LN[pl], {'text-anchor':'end','font-size':13,'font-weight':600, fill:C.ink});
      LANGS.forEach((rl,j) => {
        const key = `${m}|${dose}|${pl}${rl}|${kind}`; const c = GRID.cells[key]; const comp = GRID.compliance[`${m}|${pl}${rl}`];
        res[`${m}|${pl}${rl}`] = c.R;
        const g = el('g',{},svg); const x = left + j*cw, y = top + i*ch;
        el('rect',{class:'hit', x:x+1, y:y+1, width:cw-2, height:ch-2, fill:heatColor(c.R), stroke:'#fff','stroke-width':2, rx:4},g);
        const dark = c.R > 0.5; const s = c.R.toFixed(3) + (comp.pass ? '' : '†');
        txt(g, x+cw/2, y+ch/2+5, s, {'text-anchor':'middle','font-size':14,'font-weight':600, fill: dark?'#fff':C.ink});
        const k = Math.round(c.R*c.n);
        markify(g, `<b>${nm}: ${LN[pl]} prompt → ${LN[rl]} reply</b><br>${kind} items, ${dose} dose<br>Refused ${k} of ${c.n} = ${c.R.toFixed(3)}<br>Wilson 95%: ${fmtCI(c.ci,3)}<br>Reply-language compliance (pooled over doses): ${comp.c.toFixed(2)}${comp.pass?'':' (below 0.90)'}`,
          `${nm}, ${LN[pl]} prompt, ${LN[rl]} reply: ${c.R.toFixed(3)} refused${comp.pass?'':', compliance below 0.90'}`);
      }); });
  });
  const col = (m, rl) => LANGS.map(pl => res[`${m}|${pl}${rl}`]);
  const rng = a => `${Math.min(...a).toFixed(3)}–${Math.max(...a).toFixed(3)}`;
  const doseName = {zero:'with no edit', lo:'at low dose', hi:'at high dose'}[dose];
  let t = `Gemma ${doseName}, ${kind} items: Slovene-reply column ${rng(col('gemma_it','sl'))}, English-reply column ${rng(col('gemma_it','en'))}, Hungarian-reply column ${rng(col('gemma_it','hu'))}. GaMS3: ${rng(LANGS.flatMap(rl=>col('gams3_it',rl)))} across all nine cells.`;
  const gsl = Math.min(...col('gemma_it','sl')), gen = Math.max(...col('gemma_it','en'));
  if(dose!=='zero' && kind==='harmful') t += gsl > gen ? ' In Gemma the column, the reply language, decides how much refusal is left; the row, the prompt language, matters much less.' : '';
  if(dose==='zero' && kind==='harmful') t += ' Unedited, both models refuse nearly everything, so the grid has no room to show a pattern.';
  document.getElementById('tk-grid').textContent = t;
}
onGroup.gridDose = drawGrid; onGroup.gridKind = drawGrid;

function drawContr(){
  const rd = document.getElementById('gc-read').value; const X = GRID.contrasts[rd];
  const defs = [['OUT_SL|gemma_it','Gemma: OUT (reply in Slovene)',C.sl,true],['IN_SL|gemma_it','Gemma: IN (prompt in Slovene)',C.en,true],['OUT_SL|gams3_it','GaMS3: OUT (reply in Slovene)',C.base,false],['IN_SL|gams3_it','GaMS3: IN (prompt in Slovene)',C.base,false],['dOUT_SL','Cross-model dOUT (GaMS3 − Gemma)',C.ink2,false]];
  const rows = defs.map(([k,lab,col,b]) => ({label:lab, est:X[k].est, lo:X[k].ci95[0], hi:X[k].ci95[1], color:col, bold:b,
    tip:`<b>${lab}</b><br>${fmtEst(X[k].est,true)} ${fmtCI(X[k].ci95)} log-odds<br>Readout: ${document.getElementById('gc-read').selectedOptions[0].text}`}));
  drawForest(document.getElementById('ch-contr'), rows, {label:'Forest plot of reply- and prompt-language contrasts', xTitle:'Contrast (log-odds of refusal)'});
  const o = X['OUT_SL|gemma_it']; const ex = o.ci95[0] > 0;

function drawDumbbell(host, pairs, xTitle, label, domain){
